clue.text: Church assistant’s uniform placed in packing case

indicators.note: something placed in a box sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a crate is a wooden case used for packing goods
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A church helper's vestments arrive folded in a shipping crate.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'uniform' is not clothing but the radio-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is a junior Anglican clergyman who assists the vicar or rector of a parish.

clue.text: Instant sign of hesitation provides the impetus to move forward

blocks.note: an instant is a moment
the noise a speaker makes while hesitating

explanation.surface: A split-second pause is what gets someone going again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning a very short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the driving force or impetus that keeps a moving body or a campaign going forward.

clue.text: Utterance wears thin when uttered

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the clue's meaning

blocks.note: fabric that wears thin frays at the edges

explanation.surface: A remark repeated too often loses its force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wears thin' suggests an overused saying, but it is the verb frays, which said out loud matches a group of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a short group of words spoken or written together, so it is an utterance or expression.

clue.text: Far edges of the tarpaulin are unable to cover hotel entrance

indicators.note: the far edge of a word is its final letter, so take the end of each word
a cover wraps round what it protects, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: the final letter of this word
the final letter of this word
if you are unable you can't
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tarpaulin is too small to shelter the doorway of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a doorway, but it is the verb en-TRANCE, to put under a spell. 'Far edges' applies to both 'the' and 'tarpaulin'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to fill them with wonder and delight, which is what it means to enchant or bewitch.

clue.text: Expert in decent shape to make money

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
someone fit is in good physical condition

explanation.surface: A specialist who keeps in good condition is ready to earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In decent shape' sounds like a verdict on the expert's work, but it describes physical condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To profit is to gain financially from a deal, earning more than was spent.

clue.text: Nice seat positioned for movie buff

indicators.note: to position things is to arrange them, so these letters are placed in a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cinema lover gets a good seat in the auditorium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' could be the French city, a classic crossword trick, but here it simply supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is an enthusiast or connoisseur of films, a word borrowed from French cinéaste.

clue.text: Had fun too, weirdly without much forethought

indicators.note: done weirdly means done in an odd, irregular way, so these letters come out in a strange order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone joined in the fun impulsively, without thinking it through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weirdly' seems to describe how the fun was had, but it signals that the first three words are to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something out of hand is to do it immediately, without consideration or deliberation.

clue.text: Good downpour for wheat or corn

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a downpour is heavy rain

explanation.surface: A heavy shower of rain is just what the cereal crops need.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the usual crossword shorthand for good; 'for' simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat and corn are cereal crops, and grain is the collective term for such cereals.

clue.text: Averse to being shot?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone afraid of being hit by a bullet
setter's reading: a shot is also a photograph, so this person dislikes being photographed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: being shot here means being snapped by a photographer, not fired at.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dislikes being photographed or filmed is described as reluctant before a lens.

clue.text: Present in box that lacks plastic at the back

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end is kept
to lack something is to be without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a coffer is a strongbox for valuables
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A gift comes in a box with no plastic backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the back' looks like it places the missing plastic at the rear of the box, but it picks the last letter of 'plastic', which happens to be the box's first.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to put it forward for acceptance, which is what offering does.

clue.text: Endlessly reject encouragement

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to reject with contempt

explanation.surface: Someone keeps turning down every bit of support offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a contradiction: the word for rejecting becomes, minus one letter, a word for urging on.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is an incentive or stimulus, from the spiked device a rider uses to urge a horse on.

clue.text: Behold the stew!

blocks.note: to behold is to see
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook proudly unveils a pot of stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' reads as a noun, the dish, but the definition is the verb: to stew is to fume silently.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to brood angrily, and to seethe is to be inwardly agitated with rage; both also describe bubbling liquid.

clue.text: Favoured treatment manoeuvred me in post

indicators.note: something manoeuvred is moved around, so these letters are shifted into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits favouritism got them their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is close to &lit: a favoured relative manoeuvred into a post is exactly the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is the practice of those in power giving jobs or advantages to relatives and friends.

clue.text: Trip, start to stagger, then fall

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
to tumble is to fall

explanation.surface: A sequence of a fall: catch a foot, totter, then hit the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' could be a journey, but it is the verb, to catch one's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to catch one's foot and lose balance, which is exactly what stumbling means.

clue.text: Dessert containing coffee liqueur – or is it a rum, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters could be ordered another way

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner tastes a boozy pudding and wonders which spirit is in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like part of the question but is the link word; the anagram uses only the eight letters after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered pudding of sponge fingers soaked in espresso and liqueur, with mascarpone cream.

clue.text: Traditional wisdom is regularly also true

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A claim that old folk wisdom is often accurate too.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even-numbered letters of the last two words, starting from the L of 'also', spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is the body of knowledge and beliefs about a subject handed down orally through generations.

clue.text: Family member runs into trouble

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: bother is trouble or fuss
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A relative gets themselves into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' reads as a verb but is the abbreviation R, as on a cricket scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother is a male sibling, one of the closest relations within a family.

clue.text: Top of plant eaten by land reptile

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece is swallowed by the other

blocks.note: terrain is a stretch of land
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A tortoise on dry ground munches the tip of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land reptile' looks like one phrase, a creature of dry land, but 'land' belongs to the wordplay; ironically the answer lives mostly in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, which is a reptile.

clue.text: How performers often learn their lines using courage

definitions.text: How performers often learn their lines

blocks.note: done by something is done using it
to have heart is to have courage

explanation.surface: Actors memorise their scripts by summoning their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The long definition comes first and is descriptive rather than a single synonym; 'using' supplies the small connecting word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning something by heart means memorising it word for word, as actors do with scripts.

clue.text: Respectable, extremely tiny buildings

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: proper means respectable, socially correct
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes some small but decent houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'tiny', but it takes the word's extremes, its two end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Property means land and the buildings on it, a common estate-agent term for real estate.

clue.text: Ways to embrace love and poignant quality

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: paths are ways or routes
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A meditation on finding ways to accept love and its sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or speech that evokes pity or sadness, which makes it poignant.

clue.text: The other 22 mostly guarding central part of Belgian border

indicators.note: most but not all of a word means its last letter is cut away
the central part of a word is its middle letter, which alone is kept
a sentry stands round whatever it protects, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: the answer to the clue sharing number 22, the down entry
the fourth of seven letters sits in the middle

explanation.surface: A soldier from the other clue stands guard at the heart of Belgium's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The other 22 is 22 down, which starts in the same square as this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an edge or border, the strip along the boundary of a page or area.

clue.text: Soldier at sea, or airmen at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a seaborne fighter is navy or air force.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase 'at sea' does two jobs: literally in the definition, figuratively as the signal for a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier trained to serve on ships and fight from them, so a soldier on the ocean.

clue.text: Maybe have a drink for the lolz, say

indicators.note: to say a thing is to speak it, so we want a word with the same sound

blocks.note: lolz is internet slang for laughs, so doing something for them is doing it as a joke

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink just for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' warns that having a drink is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or liquid into the body, and drinking is one instance of that.

clue.text: Throws out various items

indicators.note: various suggests different forms, so these letters take another arrangement

blocks.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone having a clear-out discards assorted belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throws out' suggests discarding, but the definition means giving off, as a source emits light.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge something such as heat, light or sound.

clue.text: Adjust behind scope

blocks.note: the rear is what is behind
range means scope or extent

explanation.surface: An instruction to tweak a rifle's rear sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scope' suggests a telescopic gunsight, but it means extent.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to alter its order or setting, which is to rearrange it.

clue.text: Some routes to Potters Bar

indicators.note: some means only part, so the letters lie within a longer run of text

blocks.note: the last letters of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Directions to Potters Bar, a commuter town just north of London in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Potters Bar looks like a single place name, but 'Bar' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal term meaning to prevent or preclude someone from asserting a claim, so to bar.

clue.text: Over-the-top, and badly organised

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrongly, so these letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A review of an event that was both excessive and chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' is only the link; the nine letters of the last word alone are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose describes something pretentiously extravagant or showy, which is excessive or overblown.
